info.title: AVACOM Content API
info.description: Loopback API of the AVACOM Content app for the LMS. Discover the port and token in link.json (%ProgramData%\AVACOM\content\link.json). Every request needs the X-Avacom-Token header. Course content follows contracts/course.schema.json. Media are served by a second loopback server through media sessions.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code. Switch on this, never on the message.

message.description: Sentence for a log or a developer. Wording may change between versions.

details.description: Extra context when there is any, such as which parameter was rejected.

error.description: Every failure answers with this shape and nothing else.

contract.description: Major version of this API. A change here is a breaking change.

schema.description: Version of course.schema.json the installed courses were validated against.

index.description: State of the local index. While it rebuilds, catalog calls answer 503.

installedCourses.description: Courses installed and readable on this node right now.

appVersion.description: Build of the content app running on this OPS, as major.minor.patch. Ask for it before blaming the content: two classrooms can be on different builds.

code.description: Stable key inside its country tree. Never translated.

name.description: Local name to show, in the language of the country.

order.description: Sort position among its siblings. Absent means sort by name.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 of the country whose tree this course hangs from.

countryName.description: Name of that country, ready to show.

level.description: Level of the country's tree the course hangs from. In the complementary track this field holds the proficiency level instead, such as A1: the two share only their depth, so read track first.

grade.description: Grade inside that level, such as Cuarto. Only in the school track.

area.description: Area of complementary education, such as Idiomas. Only in the complementary track, where it is the widest step and takes the place the educational level has in the school tree.

subject.description: Subject of the course: Matematicas in the school tree, Ingles in the complementary one.

topic.description: Topic of the subject, and the place a course hangs from: a course IS a topic and fills one of them per language. Fracciones in the school tree, Verb to be in the complementary one.

track.description: Which tree of the country this course hangs from, and therefore which four fields describe where it sits. school: level, grade, subject and topic. complementary: area, subject, level and topic. Absent means school. Each tree uses its own four and never the other's, so a school course has no area and a complementary one has no grade.

courseId.description: Permanent id of the course. It never changes across versions: store it.

version.description: Semantic version of this release. Store it beside the courseId, because an attempt belongs to the version it was made with.

title.description: Title to show. It changes between versions, so never use it as a key.

subtitle.description: Second line of the title, when there is one.

language.description: BCP 47 tag of this course. One course file per language.

translationGroupId.description: Courses that are translations of each other share this id.

classification.description: Where the course hangs in the country's tree. The keys of /v2/tree are built out of these codes, and so is the courseId.

estimatedDurationMin.description: Minutes the whole course is expected to take.

modes.description: Modes this course can be delivered in: simple, class, exam, review, free_learning.

framework.description: Official framework such as DBA or CCSS, or a reserved AVACOM catalog.

curriculumRefs.description: Curriculum anchors of the course. This listing carries only framework and code; the course detail also carries relation.

coverMediaId.description: Media id of the cover image, to resolve through a media session.

updatedAt.description: When this version was packaged, ISO 8601 UTC.

total.description: Courses matching the filter, across every page.

kind.description: Level of the tree this node sits at: country, level, grade, subject or topic.

code.description: Stable key of the node inside its parent.

count.description: Courses hanging from this node, including its children.

children.description: Nodes one level down. A topic has none.

scope.description: What was hit: a course, a lesson, an object or a question.

lessonId.description: Lesson of the hit, when the scope reaches that deep.

objectId.description: Object of the hit, when the scope reaches that deep.

questionId.description: Question of the hit, when the scope is a question.

title.description: Title of what was hit, ready to show.

snippet.description: The hit in context, with the matched terms wrapped in ** markers. Inline Markdown, not HTML: escape it before inserting.

treePath.description: Names from the country down to the course that holds the hit, to show where it lives without asking for the tree.

total.description: Hits found, which may exceed the ones returned.

CourseOutline.description: Course metadata (see course.schema.json), lessons with object summaries {id, type, title, modes, topicRef, estimatedDurationSec, questionCount, pageCount, mediaId} curriculumNodes (the skills this course works, see CurriculumNode: the only place the catalog travels, so keep them) and previousTopics [string] (topics worth covering before this course, plain text for a teacher: a suggestion, not a reference and not a gate), media {id, kind, title, mimeType, bytes, durationSec, pageCount, width, height, altText, hasCaptions, hasTranscript, entry, simulation, license}. bytes is what the medium occupies ENCRYPTED, which is what actually travels to a device: use it to budget a preload or to report storage. It is projected from the package's signed inventory and never declared in course.json. A simulation reports the whole folder.

version.description: Version of the course this pool came from. Store it with the attempt.

settings.description: Selection and delivery settings, so the LMS can assemble a balanced exam.

questionId.description: Id of the question inside the course.

type.description: One of the six question kinds.

topicRef.description: Topic the question measures. Required inside an exam, and what coverAllTopics balances against.

difficulty.description: From 1, very easy, to 5, very hard. Used to balance one exam against another.

estimatedSec.description: Seconds the question is expected to take. The exam time limit adds these up when the exam declares extraPercent.

questions.description: Every question available, with the metadata needed to pick, and no answer keys.

title.description: Title of the exam, ready to show.

instructions.description: What the student reads before starting.

items.description: Question without answer keys, feedback or teacher notes

questions.description: Questions in the order requested, redacted: no key ever comes out of here.

prompt.description: The prompt, repeated so the teacher does not have to look it up.

responseFormat.description: How the student answered: text, drawing or audio.

modelAnswer.description: An answer that would earn full marks. For the teacher only.

rubric.description: Criteria with their points and bands.

incorrectExamples.description: Answers anticipated as wrong, with the reason each one fails.

courseId.description: Course of the question being evaluated.

version.description: Optional. Defaults to the installed version; archived versions allowed.

objectId.description: Object the question belongs to. It decides whether keys may be shown.

response.description: multiple_choice {selectedOptionIds[]}, true_false {value}, fill_blanks {blanks:{id:value}}, matching {pairs:[{leftId,rightId}]}, ordering {order[]}, drag_drop {placements:[{itemId,targetId}]}, open {text|drawingRef|audioRef}

score.description: Points earned, rounded to four decimals with banker's rounding.

correct.description: Whether the answer counts as right. With partial credit it can be false and still score.

requiresManualGrading.description: True for an open question: the app never grades prose.

feedback.description: What to show the student, chosen from what the content declared for this mistake.

example.feedback: Bien: el vapor se enfria y vuelve a liquido.

courseId.description: Course whose media will be served.

lessonId.description: Open a session for every medium of this lesson. Use it instead of listing ids one by one.

mediaIds.description: Specific media to open, when a whole lesson is more than needed.

ttlSec.description: Seconds the session stays valid. It expires on its own; a class never needs hours.

sessionId.description: Id of the session, to revoke it when the class ends.

baseUrl.description: Loopback base the media server answers on. The port changes between runs.

expiresAt.description: When the session stops answering. ISO 8601 UTC with second precision, always ending in Z, like every other timestamp of this API.

urls.description: mediaId to URL. Simulations point to their entry file; relative resources resolve under the same folder.

files.description: Simulations only. GET returns {mediaId, entry, files[]} with every relative path of the simulation folder; each file is served at <baseUrl><mediaId>/<path>.

poster.description: Videos with a posterPath only: <baseUrl><mediaId>/@poster, the still image shown before playback, served with its own image type. Optional and additive: absent or null when the medium declares no poster.

extras.description: Per mediaId: captions (VTT) and transcript for audio and video, poster image for videos that declare one, files list URL for simulations.

id.description: Stable id of the node. It is what curriculumRefs points at, it never changes, and it is shared between courses: store it as the aggregation key.

name.description: The node in the words a teacher would use, in the language of the curriculum. Show this, never the id.

parent.description: The broader node this one belongs to. Absent means it is the top of its branch. Mastery rolls up along this chain.

type.description: What the node is in the tree of its education level. The first six are levels and go from broad to narrow in that order; the last three hang at the end of a branch. Absent means skill.

replaces.description: Node ids this one superseded when the curriculum redrew them. Evidence gathered under those ids keeps counting for this node; nothing new should be anchored to them.

order.description: Where the node goes among its siblings, from 0. Absent means sort by name.

CurriculumNode.description: A node of the AVACOM curriculum catalog. The catalog is the sum of what the installed courses declare: there is no central list to ask for, and GET /v2/curriculum serves what this machine has.

courses.description: Installed courses that declare this node.

children.description: Nodes that hang from this one.

CurriculumCatalogNode.description: A node of the catalog as this machine knows it, with the courses that declare it and the nodes below.

nodeId.description: Node this anchor points at. It can be an id the asked-for node superseded, which is how old content keeps answering.

scope.description: What is anchored: the course, a lesson, an object or a question.

refId.description: Id of the anchored piece inside the course.

relation.description: teaches, assesses, or absent when the content did not declare it. Absent must not be read as either.

lessonId.description: Lesson the piece belongs to, when it is a lesson, an object or a question.

objectId.description: Object the piece belongs to, when it is an object or a question.

objectType.description: Type of that object: lecture, explanation, simulation_lab, activity or exam.

title.description: Title to show: the object's, the lesson's or the course's, whichever the anchor is on.

CurriculumAnchor.description: One anchor of installed content to a node of the curriculum catalog.

code.description: Code of the check that failed: E-PKG-FORMAT (no package.json, or not an AVACOMPKG2 package), E-PKG-PUBLISHER-UNTRUSTED (the publisher key is not trusted by this device), E-PKG-SIGNATURE (the signed inventory was altered), E-PKG-HASH (a file differs in size or hash), E-PKG-INVENTORY (a file of the signed inventory is missing, or a file not in it is present), E-PKG-LICENSE (no licence for this device or this build), E-PKG-COURSE (course.json cannot be decrypted, is invalid or does not match package.json), E-PKG-COURSE-MEDIA (course.json names a media file the package does not carry) or E-PKG-MISSING (indexed, but its folder is gone). E-PKG-VERSION and E-PKG-IO are install outcomes and never appear here.

message.description: What failed, in English and naming the file when there is one.

IntegrityProblem.description: One thing wrong with an installed package.

packageKey.description: Key of the installed package: courseId@version.

title.description: Course title, to show without a second call.

status.description: ok when every check passed, broken when one failed, missing when the folder is in the index but not on disk.

deep.description: Whether every file was read and hashed. False means only sizes, signature, licence and course.json were checked.

files.description: Files on disk inside the package.

bytes.description: What the package occupies on disk, in bytes.

checkedAt.description: When this answer was produced, ISO 8601 UTC. Nothing is cached: it is the moment of the call.

problems.description: Empty when the status is ok.

PackageIntegrity.description: The integrity of one installed package, checked at the moment of the call.
